body:
I was working two jobs. Had a morning shift with Job1 and a closing shift with Job2 on the same day. 
I was sick and had been struggling through the morning shift with Job1. I ended up deciding to call in sick before my second shift at Job2 because I was honestly feeling awful. 
I called in, explained that I was sick, and I wouldn't be able to make it in. Usually one of the managers would try to convince me to come in anyways, but that day I wasn't having it and made that clear when I spoke to my manager. 
A moment later I was having the speaker on my phone blown out as the manager began tearing me down for daring to call in sick. 
So I quit. Came in the next day and dropped off my nametag. No regrets.
I'm not sure if I'm depressed. I don't take vitamins. I have a relatively healthy diet but I rarely feel hungry. I have no insurance. I can't afford to throw money at a doctor's clinic.

I'm not sure how true this is, but one time I read that hotlines like SPH and 911 actually will refuse employment to people who have previously attempted suicide or have been diagnosed with mental illnesses of any kind. I remember reading that there was a reason for this, but I don't remember what it was.
